headline: What Trump’s Summit in China Reveals

paragraphs.text: Editor’s Note: Washington Week With The Atlantic is a partnership between NewsHour Productions, WETA, and The Atlantic airing every Friday on PBS stations nationwide. Check your local listings, watch full episodes here, or listen to the weekly podcast here.

President Trump is back in Washington after a week in Asia, where he met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. On Washington Week With The Atlantic, panelists joined to discuss the summit and more.

When Trump arrived in China, he was greeted on the tarmac by Xi. “For somebody who is so concerned with optics, who has been so built around the idea of his own personal image, I think that actually does play a lot into this,” Adam Haris, the host of Radio Atlantic, said of Trump last night. But, Harris argued, while the president conducts a “shaking-hands-and-slapping-back sort of diplomacy,” the rest of the world “acknowledges that this isn’t necessarily anything but smoke.”

Joining the editor in chief of The Atlantic, Jeffrey Goldberg, to discuss this and more: Susan Glasser, a staff writer at The New Yorker; Harris; Liz Landers, a White House correspondent at PBS News; and Nancy Youssef, a staff writer at The Atlantic.
